subject: Persistent 504 surge — queue backlog and KV-cache eviction causing retry loop
messages:
From: Kate Turner <kate.turner@rivex.io>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: sudden 504s / timeouts on inference endpoints

Ben —

We're seeing a sharp uptick in 504s and timeouts across our inference calls to your hosted API starting around 08:45 PT. Error rate jumped from ~0.2% to ~6% and tail latency is spiking to >12s. This is impacting our checkout scoring flow (sync path).

Attached a small sample of failing request IDs and timestamps. Our client has exponential backoff but appears to be amplifying the load (we're seeing repeated retries). Can you confirm whether this is on your side or our integration? We need a quick mitigation and a timeline for a fix — our ops team is standing by.

Thanks,
Kate
Kate Turner
Head of Platform, Rivex

Attachments: sample-requests.json (10 items)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Kate Turner <kate.turner@rivex.io>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 09:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: sudden 504s / timeouts on inference endpoints

Kate —

Thanks for the heads up and the request samples. I'm looping in SRE (Monica) and your CSM (Rishi) so we can triage immediately. Initial ask: can you share the client retry settings (max attempts, backoff) and whether you started any traffic surge or rollout at ~08:30 PT?

We'll triage and come back with a mitigation plan within 60 minutes. Apologies for the disruption.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kate Turner <kate.turner@rivex.io>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 09:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: sudden 504s / timeouts on inference endpoints

Ben / Rishi / Kate —

Investigation notes (quick):
- We see a sharp increase in queue length on the frontend routing layer for the us-west cluster servicing Rivex.
- KV-cache eviction rate spiked at 08:42; prefix-cache miss ratio went from ~6% to ~48% in 3 minutes.
- Batcher queue depth rose to >1200 pending requests; worker saturation observed leading to >10s head-of-queue waits.
- Significant retry amplification: a subset of clients are retrying with minimal backoff and duplicate requests are exacerbating queueing.

Immediate mitigations performed (09:32):
- Toggled aggressive per-account soft-queue limit for Rivex to prevent further queue-accrual (temporary).
- Disabled prefix-KV caching for the Rivex routing shard (to avoid eviction thrash while SRE digs in).
- Increased the worker pool on the affected pool by 30% (hotfix).

We attached the eviction and worker logs (kv-eviction-20270412.log). Next steps: deep dive into why prefix entries were evicted rapidly (possible bug in prefix key hashing after recent kernel optimization), reproduce in staging. I recommend a short maintenance window to roll a patch and re-enable cache.

I'll update ASAP once we have root cause.

—Monica
Monica Patel | SRE, Redwood Inference

Attachments: kv-eviction-20270412.log

Kate —

Thanks for your patience. We've temporarily disabled the prefix-KV cache and applied safeguards to reduce retry amplification. Monica and the SRE team will push a targeted fix during a short maintenance window.

Can you confirm that the temporary measures restore acceptable error rates on your side? If so, we'll schedule the patch and a postmortem. Separately, customer asks:
- Do you want a proactive credits adjustment for today's incident?
- Would you like an executive briefing (CTO + VP Sales) tomorrow?

Planned maintenance (proposal):
- UTC 2027-04-13 02:00–03:00 (US evening) — apply patch to prefix hashing + revert cache toggle
- Rollback plan: immediate toggle off and scale worker pool if issues recur

Rishi

3) Executive briefing: Markus (CTO) and Laura (VP Sales) are available for a 30-minute call tomorrow at 11:00 PT to walk through root cause and mitigations. Please let me know if that works.
